    <item>
      <title>US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan</link>
      <description><p>DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.</p><p>Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie and his church set up sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children, say prosecutors</p><p>A Kenyan court has found the starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of ⁠190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult-related disasters in recent history.</p><p>Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast ⁠in south-eastern Kenya.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Witness says drone struck twice at transport hub in al-Dibab, in one of deadliest single attacks of war</p><p>A drone strike near a market in southern Sudan on Sunday evening killed 80 people, mostly commuters catching rides home.</p><p>Ahmed Wadi, a witness, said the attack in the town of al-Dibab in West Kordofan state left “50 bodies who I helped bury, one of them my own brother Mohamed”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/drone-attack-market-al-dibab-west-kordofan-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Ebola cases in Kenya highlight US failures amid Trump cuts to key services</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/ebola-cases-kenya-us-quarantine</link>
      <description><p>Opposition to US-led quarantine center in Kenya follows sweeping funding cuts and withdrawal from WHO</p><p>An eighth person in Kenya has tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the country’s first-ever cluster of cases of the virus, as the second-largest outbreak in history has killed more than 4,300 and sickened more than 9,000 people in the region.</p><p>It highlights the diminished role the US has played in the worsening Ebola outbreak by building a controversial quarantine center in Kenya, pulling back health support globally, and banning travelers from certain countries. All of this has also reduced the ability to identify and respond to the outbreak and exacerbated mistrust.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/ebola-cases-kenya-us-quarantine">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype</link>
      <description><p>Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowds</p><p>For the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on.</p><p>His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:41:52 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><title>🔴 French PM vows 'massive' police operation for new protests on Saturday</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261020-live-curfews-come-into-effect-around-france-to-combat-looting</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">793f3954-cc8b-11f1-8e8f-2b6c5c6d0fa2</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:38:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title><![CDATA[France's sociopolitical & economic crises: 'Large portion of population sympathizes' with protestors]]></title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261020-france-s-sociopolitical-economic-crises-large-portion-of-population-sympathizes-with-protestors</link><description>
Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Damien Lecomte, Political Scientist and Researcher at Paris Panthéon Sorbonne University. France’s escalating unrest has exposed a profound contradiction in the state’s response: disproportionate force against peaceful demonstrators and an inability to contain widespread violence. As competing narratives threaten to overshadow legitimate grievances over education, public services and the cost of living, he warns that the "repressive response won't make the social crisis disappear.” With presidential elections approaching, the struggle to restore order is becoming inseparable from a deeper contest over political legitimacy, public liberties and the future direction of French society.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f11ae6d6-cc80-11f1-aaa1-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261020-130312-130947-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f11ae6d6-cc80-11f1-aaa1-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261020-130312-130947-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f670fe18-cc80-11f1-a285-b9e456527e5c</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:32:09 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>Six years on, France remembers slain teacher Samuel Paty</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20261020-six-years-on-france-remembers-slain-teacher-samuel-paty</link><description>
French schoolteacher Samuel Paty was killed on October 16, 2020 after false rumours circulated about racism following one of his lessons in which cartoons from the satirical publication Charlie Hebdo were shown. For the first time since his murder, journalists from France Télévisions were allowed to film inside the school where he taught in Conflans-Sainte-Honorine, near Paris. They met a new generation of young people, who are determined to play their part in the fight against terrorism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/07dd9088-cbd9-11f1-b486-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-NW-OOV-ECRAN-ECR-FRZ-SAMUEL-PATY-MARCHAIS-Florent.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/07dd9088-cbd9-11f1-b486-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-NW-OOV-ECRAN-ECR-FRZ-SAMUEL-PATY-MARCHAIS-Florent.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">435e5476-cbd9-11f1-bd0c-4b8fae061dce</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:28:07 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Florent MARCHAIS</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ivorian DJ digs forgotten tracks, on the hunt for great classics</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261020-ivorian-dj-digs-forgotten-tracks-on-the-hunt-for-great-classics</link><description>
Cédric Kouamé travels across Ivory Coast to collect old vinyl records before restoring them. The Ivorian DJ hopes to bring national attention to his passion through an official centre dedicated to the country's historical archives, as FRANCE 24's team on the ground reports.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e84694e-cc82-11f1-9ed1-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-40128c7c.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e84694e-cc82-11f1-9ed1-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-40128c7c.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">47159f18-cc81-11f1-a7d9-1be4b0761cb5</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:09:36 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Midterms 2026: The farmers calling for more migrant workers</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261020-midterms-2026-the-farmers-calling-for-more-migrant-workers</link><description>
As the US midterms approach, immigration is once again dominating the country’s political discourse and Arizona’s largely agricultural Yuma County, just miles from the Mexican border, is no exception. But here, farmers like John Boelts are calling for more legal migrants, warning that without the labour they provide essential crops may go to waste or never be planted at all. France 24’s Sam Ball and Barbara Gabel sent this report.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2e2330d6-cbd4-11f1-a9eb-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/main-dans-les-champs.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2e2330d6-cbd4-11f1-a9eb-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/main-dans-les-champs.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a023b876-cc84-11f1-ba8e-65b2a060ce5b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:09:22 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Tue, 20 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Could a $200K bond for satellites paid before launch prevent a space junk disaster in orbit? Here's why some scientists think so ]]> The space around Earth is turning into a junkyard. Researchers think a refundable deposit scheme could force satellite operators to clean up their act before a tipping point is reached.

For years, space sustainability experts have warned that the growing number of satellites in orbit and the quantity of dead metal left behind threatens to trigger a dangerous cascade of collisions known as the Kessler Syndrome. Predicted in the 1970s by NASA physicist Donald Kessler, this chain of orbital smashups could make the space around Earth unusable and unsafe.

The dangerous tipping might be nearer than some think. Humankind's utilization of space is at an inflection point, as companies such as SpaceX, Blue Origin and Amazon plan to launch constellations of hundreds of thousands of telecommunication satellites and orbiting data centers in the coming years.

"Low Earth orbit looks like lots of other resources that we have trashed as economic actors," Daniel Kaffine, a professor of environmental and resource economics at University of Colorado Boulder, told Space.com.

"Waiting until it gets really, really bad to start implementing any of these types of policy interventions has historically been what we have done," Kaffine added. "But maybe we can think about things we can do right now."

In a paper published last month in the journal Nature Communications, Kaffine and his collaborators propose a scheme that would require satellite operators to post a bond of $200,000 before launch, refundable with interest upon the completion of a successful deorbit. Companies that fail to remove their junk would lose the money, which could go toward a shared pool funding active debris-removal missions, the researchers said.

"You could possibly raise billions of dollars by that," said Kaffine. "We think it's a very neat policy that doesn't require international coordination."

International bodies, such as the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee, ask satellite operators to remove their spacecraft from orbit within 25 years after the mission's end. The American Federal Communications Commission (FCC) imposes an even stricter standard — a five-year requirement for satellites in low Earth orbit. Still, a staggering 60% of satellites remain in place when their propellant runs out, the researchers say, as no consequences ensue if they fail to deorbit.

Solving the problem on the international level would be difficult, as international bodies have no powers to enforce compliance. Moreover, the United Nations Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space (COPUOS), which sets down rules for the peaceful exploration of outer space, requires the unanimous support of every member state to pass new regulations, which is nearly impossible to achieve.

"The policy we propose could be implemented on a national level, which is why we think it's interesting," Indigo Brownhall, a space sustainability researcher at University College London and the paper's lead author, told Space.com. "Any country in Europe can request satellites registered with them to follow this bond policy."

To put it simply, no satellite registered in a given country gets to space before putting the money into the kitty. The researchers acknowledge that it might be hard to persuade major players historically averse to regulations, such as the U.S., to roll out such a scheme. But they say a more environmentally conscious block, like the European Union (EU), could enforce compliance by limiting market access to those who observe their rules.

"The consumer market in Europe is massive, like 300 to 400 million people," Brownhall said. "And the EU can request anyone who wants to sell space data or any products in the EU to follow their rules. They did this with GDPR [General Data Protection Regulation]. And you can imagine that somebody like Starlink [SpaceX's satellite-internet subsidiary] surely wants to sell Starlink terminals to Europeans."

The authors estimate that, even if the scheme only covered 20% of global satellite launches, it would reduce the number of derelict satellites careening around the planet by 18%.

Currently, more than 57,000 pieces of space debris larger than 4 inches (10 centimeters) hurtle around Earth completely out of control, according to estimates by the European Space Agency. That's double the figure from less than 10 years ago. Most of these fragments were generated by explosions and orbital collisions that shattered satellites and used rocket stages into clouds of dangerous debris.

"Leaving big satellites that no longer work up there is like a ticking time bomb," Brownhall said. "Active satellites can move out of the way, but when two derelict satellites are going to hit each other, there is nothing you can do but watch it."

Kaffine said the policy could be modelled on U.S. oil operators' bond scheme, in place since the 1960s, which ensures that oil giants plug used oil wells after ceasing extraction.

"If the oil operators clean up after completing the oil production job, they get the money back," said Kaffine. "If they don't, the money goes into a fund, which the government then uses to clean up orphan wells. It's quite an analogous situation to what we see in space."

In the meantime, evidence of the worsening orbital situation is coming thick and fast. Space situational awareness companies such as U.S.-based LeoLabs, which use networks of ground-based radars and telescopes to monitor traffic in space, report increasing numbers of disintegration events — incidents involving either an explosion or a collision between old satellites, fragments and rocket bodies. In the past six months, LeoLabs has reported at least four fragmentation events in space, which together created hundreds of new pieces of space debris.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX launches its 'Starfall' return capsule for 2nd time ever (video) ]]>

SpaceX just launched its mysterious "Starfall" return capsule for the second time ever.

Starfall was one of 32 payloads on the company's Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission, which launched atop a Falcon 9 rocket at 7:04 a.m. EDT (1104 GMT) today (Oct. 20) from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

SpaceX has been relatively quiet about Starfall, which debuted this past June on a Falcon 9 launch from the Cape.

That June 23 flight was a dedicated demonstration mission for Starfall, designed to show that the capsule can fly in a controlled fashion and survive the harrowing downward trip through Earth's atmosphere.

And those will be Starfall's main jobs. The vehicle "will enable affordable, routine access to the microgravity environment for scientific research and in-space manufacturing," SpaceX in a June 23 X post, one of the few public statements the company has made about Starfall.

Indeed, most of the details that we have about the capsule come from an environmental assessment that was published by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration in May.

According to that document, the disk-shaped Starfall is roughly 2.5 feet (0.75 meters) tall and 10.2 feet (3.1 m) wide. It weighs about 4,600 pounds (2,100 kilograms) and can bring 2,200 pounds (1,000 kg) of payload back down to Earth.

Starfall wasn't the only return capsule that went up on Bandwagon-5. Among the other 31 payloads on the flight was W-Series 7, the latest orbital "mini-factory" built and operated by the California company Varda Space Industries.

The W-Series capsules are designed to both host the production of valuable goods such as pharmaceuticals and bring them safely down to Earth, Varda has said.

The other payloads on Bandwagon-5 are a mix of "cubesats and microsats," according to SpaceX's mission description. Among the latter is Pelican-12, a sharp-eyed Earth-observation satellite built by the San Francisco company Planet.

If all goes according to plan today, the 32 payloads will be deployed over a nearly two-hour span beginning about 57 minutes after launch. Starfall will be the last to separate, releasing from the Falcon 9's upper stage two hours and 48 minutes post-liftoff.

The Falcon 9's first stage, meanwhile, came back to Earth as planned on Bandwagon-5. It touched down about nine minutes after launch, coming down in the Atlantic Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "A Shortfall of Gravitas." It was the 19th mission for this particular booster, according to the company.

Bandwagon is one of two SpaceX rideshare programs. The other, known as Transporter, has been busier, flying 18 missions to date.

The first Transporter mission, which lifted off in January 2021, delivered 143 payloads to Earth orbit, a single-launch record that still stands.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA closes the book on epic OSIRIS-REx asteroid-sampling mission: 'I am immensely proud of what we did' ]]> On Sept. 30, NASA formally concluded OSIRIS-REx, the historic first U.S. mission to pluck a pristine piece of an asteroid and deliver it safely back to Earth.

The van-sized OSIRIS-REx spacecraft — whose name is short for Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer — visited and sampled Bennu, an ancient space rock holding pristine remnants from the dawn of our solar system more than 4.5 billion years ago. Among those cosmic relics are raw organic building blocks, the kind that may have seeded life on Earth.

"I have known this day was coming for a long time, but it is still difficult to see it arrive," OSIRIS-REx Principal Investigator Dante Lauretta, who's based at the University of Arizona, said in a post on LinkedIn. "I feel enormous pride in what we accomplished together, and real sadness that this journey has come to an end."

For the mission team, the farewell capped a decade of high-stakes engineering, on-the-fly troubleshooting and nail-biting close calls that ultimately delivered to Earth the largest asteroid sample ever collected in space, one that held secrets from the early solar system.

Long before launch, the team faced obstacles that nearly thwarted the endeavor — chiefly, two rejections from NASA — before finally securing the green light for the $1 billion project under the New Frontiers Program in 2011.

When OSIRIS-REx launched on Sept. 8, 2016, on a two-year journey across the inner solar system, Bennu was little more than a point of light in telescopes. Scientists expected the asteroid’s surface to be a smooth, sandy sphere where OSIRIS-REx could seamlessly touch down. Much to their surprise, however, when the probe arrived at the asteroid in late 2018, it revealed Bennu to be a treacherous, loosely bound amalgamation of jagged boulders.

"Our expectations about the asteroid's surface were completely wrong," Lauretta said in an Oct. 7 statement from the University of Arizona. "There was no obvious place to collect a sample anywhere."

When OSIRIS-REx touched down on a small crater named Nightingale, Bennu offered so little structural resistance that scientists said its surface reacted more like fluid than a hard, rocky shell. The spacecraft's sampling head sank directly into the asteroid, stopping after burrowing 20 inches (51 centimeters) deep by firing its thrusters at the right time to pull away, with the precious sample in hand.

Then came another nail-biting moment: The sample collector lid got jammed in a partially open position because so much material was scooped up, allowing fragments of the precious cargo to escape. In a race against time to prevent further loss, the mission team quickly stowed the sampler head directly inside the return capsule, securing the cosmic treasure for its journey back to Earth.

Even the final return to Earth, on Sept. 24, 2023, kept the team on edge: A parachute failed to deploy properly during reentry, forcing a tense but ultimately safe landing in the Utah desert.

"Successful exploration missions are not those that avoid surprises; they are those that are deliberately designed to adapt to them," Lauretta said in the statement, quoting a line from the mission's final report to NASA.

"That certainly describes OSIRIS-REx," he said. "Again and again, the mission presented us with circumstances we had not expected, and again and again, this team found a way forward."

The mission's triumphs began long before the samples reached Earth. For example, the probe set a Guinness World Record when it slid into orbit around the 1,610-foot-wide (490 meters) Bennu, which became the smallest object ever circled by a spacecraft.

The scientific payoff that followed included remote-sensing work that confirmed Bennu's surface is coated in carbon-bearing compounds. Those observations also revealed that Bennu was once part of a much larger, water-rich parent asteroid that shattered in a catastrophic collision in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

The returned sample — which weighs 4.29 ounces (121.6 grams) here on Earth, more than twice the mission's requirement — continues to thrill and occupy scientists.

A wave of research papers, now topping 200, continues to piece together the composition and history of the ancient space rock. Among other findings, Bennu's pristine material has revealed amino acids and sugars that, on Earth, are essential for life, alongside a history of exposure to liquid water that could have served as the "broth" for these compounds to interact.

More discoveries are likely to come. Most of the returned Bennu sample is being preserved for future generations of scientists, who will study it "with questions and instruments we cannot yet anticipate," Lauretta said in the statement.

Though its OSIRIS-REx chapter is closed, the spacecraft itself is far from retired. Renamed OSIRIS-APEX (OSIRIS-APophis EXplorer), the probe is using its remaining propellant to head toward Apophis, another near-Earth asteroid and a different type of space rock from Bennu. It is scheduled to arrive in 2029.

"I feel enormous pride in what we accomplished together, and real sadness that this journey has come to an end."

For the mission team, the farewell capped a decade of high-stakes engineering, on-the-fly troubleshooting and nail-biting close calls that ultimately delivered to Earth the largest asteroid sample ever collected in space, one that held secrets from the early solar system.

Long before launch, the team faced obstacles that nearly thwarted the endeavor — chiefly, two rejections from NASA — before finally securing the green light for the $1 billion project under the New Frontiers Program in 2011.

When OSIRIS-REx launched on Sept. 8, 2016, on a two-year journey across the inner solar system, Bennu was little more than a point of light in telescopes. Scientists expected the asteroid’s surface to be a smooth, sandy sphere where OSIRIS-REx could seamlessly touch down. Much to their surprise, however, when the probe arrived at the asteroid in late 2018, it revealed Bennu to be a treacherous, loosely bound amalgamation of jagged boulders.

"Our expectations about the asteroid's surface were completely wrong," Lauretta said in an Oct. 7 statement from the University of Arizona. "There was no obvious place to collect a sample anywhere."

When OSIRIS-REx touched down on a small crater named Nightingale, Bennu offered so little structural resistance that scientists said its surface reacted more like fluid than a hard, rocky shell. The spacecraft's sampling head sank directly into the asteroid, stopping after burrowing 20 inches (51 centimeters) deep by firing its thrusters at the right time to pull away, with the precious sample in hand.

Then came another nail-biting moment: The sample collector lid got jammed in a partially open position because so much material was scooped up, allowing fragments of the precious cargo to escape. In a race against time to prevent further loss, the mission team quickly stowed the sampler head directly inside the return capsule, securing the cosmic treasure for its journey back to Earth.

Even the final return to Earth, on Sept. 24, 2023, kept the team on edge: A parachute failed to deploy properly during reentry, forcing a tense but ultimately safe landing in the Utah desert.

"Successful exploration missions are not those that avoid surprises; they are those that are deliberately designed to adapt to them," Lauretta said in the statement, quoting a line from the mission's final report to NASA.

"That certainly describes OSIRIS-REx," he said. "Again and again, the mission presented us with circumstances we had not expected, and again and again, this team found a way forward."

The mission's triumphs began long before the samples reached Earth. For example, the probe set a Guinness World Record when it slid into orbit around the 1,610-foot-wide (490 meters) Bennu, which became the smallest object ever circled by a spacecraft.

The scientific payoff that followed included remote-sensing work that confirmed Bennu's surface is coated in carbon-bearing compounds. Those observations also revealed that Bennu was once part of a much larger, water-rich parent asteroid that shattered in a catastrophic collision in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

The returned sample — which weighs 4.29 ounces (121.6 grams) here on Earth, more than twice the mission's requirement — continues to thrill and occupy scientists.

A wave of research papers, now topping 200, continues to piece together the composition and history of the ancient space rock. Among other findings, Bennu's pristine material has revealed amino acids and sugars that, on Earth, are essential for life, alongside a history of exposure to liquid water that could have served as the "broth" for these compounds to interact.

More discoveries are likely to come. Most of the returned Bennu sample is being preserved for future generations of scientists, who will study it "with questions and instruments we cannot yet anticipate," Lauretta said in the statement.

Though its OSIRIS-REx chapter is closed, the spacecraft itself is far from retired. It is scheduled to arrive in 2029.

]]> <![CDATA[ The X-Files Lego set is a wonderful bit of 90s sci-fi nostalgia ]]> Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell.

One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi, when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services. You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set.

This 1478 piece set is essentially two dioramas crammed into a single display piece. The top of the model depicts a spinning UFO floating above one of those iconic coniferous forests that dominated 90s sci-fi. Why? Because — thanks to some generous tax credits — it was cheaper to shoot in Vancouver, so that's where they all flocked.

Disney Plus / Hulu bundle: was $12.99 now $11.99
Catch Mulder and Scully in every season of The X-Files on Hulu, which is available bundled with Disney+ for only $11.99/month for the first six months, then increasing to $12.99/month.View Deal

Beneath the woodland scene, though, is the real star of the show: Mulder's office, squirrelled away in the basement of the FBI's J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D.C. This dingy little office is where Scully meets "Spooky Mulder", kicking off a glorious sci-fi odyssey that would last for eleven seasons (and two movies).

Mulder's dingy little base of operations has been stunningly recreated here, with both overt references and subtle nods that X-Files fans will appreciate. The iconic "I want to believe" poster adorns the wall, alongside photographs of crop circles and a newspaper clipping from a paper called "The Lone Brickman" — a nice nod to "The Lone Gunmen". There's even an actual X-File sitting on the desk, and a cute Lego spoof of the "Face on Mars", with a photo on the wall that shows a Lego head on the moon.

The X-Files Complete Boxset: $160
Prefer to actually own your media? Make your way through this X-Files Complete Boxset on DVD. Just bear in mind that you will need a region-free DVD player to watch it with.

It's been a hot minute since I watched The X-Files (that DVD box set beside my TV is calling to me), but even so, I had a blast building my way down memory lane, remembering episodes as I assembled the diorama. I love the little touches, like the display cabinets filled with artifacts, the VHS tapes scattered around the office and the black oil spillage on the floor.

As with most Lego sets, the minifigures are half the joy. You get Mulder and Scully, obviously, with the dynamic duo of FBI agents both rocking flashlights (no smartphones with built-in lights back in the 90s). Mulder is wearing dark blue, while Scully is rocking an orangey brown suit, with both of them sporting an FBI badge.

Outside of the principal pair, you also get Skinner, Mr X, and the Cigarette Smoking Man. Mulder's partner-turned-nemesis Alex Krycek also gets a suitably devious-looking minifig. It's the gloves, they just make him look like a bad man (which, to be fair, he is). Finally, to ramp up the paranormal scale, we also get a pair of monster minifigs: a grey alien and Flukeman minifigures. The grey alien was a must-have, especially given the UFO floating atop this display piece, but the one-off monster of the week, Flukeman, felt like a weird choice.

Also, this John Doggett erasure will not stand. Sure, he could never replace Mulder, but Robert Patrick's seasons eight and nine run was excellent and he deserved a spot here.

And while I'm voicing minor gripes, the usual Lego FOMO tricks were in force with this set; if you pre-ordered, you got an exclusive gift set — Scully's Lab — free of charge. This extra little diorama isn't necessary, but it does feel like the collection is incomplete without it and it's not for sale separately, so you'll have to try your luck with eBay scalpers if you want it.

Speaking of Scully, Gillian Anderson has stated that after season 11 wrapped in 2018, she was done with the role. That wasn't entirely accurate, though, as she donned the lab gloves one more time for the Lego X-Files set advert. It's a short bit of fan service, but a nice touch, and, once again, it sparks those 90s neurons.

All these delicious Member Berries come at a price, though, and that's the price. This blast from the past will set you back $199 (£179 in the UK). That's no small chunk of change. But then again, anyone who wants this set is in their thirties or forties and can probably afford that outlay for the nostalgia trip. And look at it this way: when The X-Files debuted back in 1993, the price would only have been about $86.

I had a great time building the Lego X-Files set and if you're a fan of the series, you will too. Nostalgia often feels like a cheat code to our hearts, but there's nothing wrong with that. We deserve to remember the good times and the truth is that The X-Files was about as good as it ever got for sci-fi fans.

You can buy the Lego X-Files set now, available for $199/£179 from the Lego store.

]]> <![CDATA[ Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video) ]]>

Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt.

The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20).

The JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency)-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos. If everything goes according to plan, MMX will become the first spacecraft to land on and return samples from Phobos for study back on Earth, which scientists think could shed light on a decades-old mystery about the moons' origins and reveal clues about the formation of the early solar system.

It was the 10th liftoff of Japan's expendable, two-stage H3 rocket, which was jointly developed by JAXA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. After clearing its launch pad today, the 207-foot-tall (63 meters) launch vehicle flew a nominal trajectory through its ascent corridor over the Pacific Ocean, jettisoning its four solid boosters in pairs just before the flight clock reached two minutes. The rocket shed its payload fairings about one minute and 20 seconds later, exposing MMX to the vacuum of space for the first time.

H3's first stage, powered by two LE-9 rocket engines, channels a mixture of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen to produce a combined thrust of 331,000 pounds (1,471 kN), according to Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. As the mission clock approached T+5 minutes, H3 executed its main engine cutoff procedure and separated from the second stage, which ignited its engines for a 5.5-minute burn about 10 seconds later.

All continued to go to plan after that. The H3's upper stage ignited its engine for a second time for a trans-Mars injection burn about one hour and four minutes after liftoff, a maneuver that lasted roughly six minutes and 25 seconds and took MMX to a maximum velocity of about 24,145 mph (38,858 kph).

MMX was released from the rocket's upper stage right on schedule, about one minute after the completion of that burn and roughly 71 minutes after liftoff. The success elicited loud cheers in mission control, which viewers saw and heard on JAXA's launch webcast.

MMX is now under its own power, and on course for Mars. The interplanetary transit will last about 10 months, with the spacecraft scheduled to arrive at the Red Planet in August 2027. When it does, MMX's propulsion module will execute an orbital insertion burn to place itself in a quasi-satellite orbit (QSO) around Phobos, which places MMX within the space around the moon as both circle Mars.

MMX will spend about three years in the Martian system, devoting much of that time to studying the 14-mile-wide (22 km) Phobos with its science instruments. The spacecraft also carries the IDEFIX rover, a joint effort of the space agencies of France and Germany, which is scheduled to deploy to the surface of Phobos in late 2028 or early 2029.

After a mapping campaign to select suitable landing sites, MMX will perform two separate touchdowns on Phobos to collect and stow samples in the spacecraft's return capsule. Following its second landing and sample collection, MMX will briefly return to QSO with Phobos before transferring to a more elongated orbit around Mars that intersects with the planet's smaller moon, Deimos, which is just 8 miles (14 km) in diameter.

During the last several months of its time around Mars, MMX will perform a series of Deimos flybys before departing for Earth in November 2030. If all goes according to plan, the MMX sample-return capsule will land in Australia in 2031.

Scientists are counting on those samples, and other data collected during MMX's time around Mars, to answer a decades-old question surrounding the Martian moons' origins. Competing theories and conflicting evidence point to two possibilities for how Mars got its moons.

Their near-circular, equatorial orbits suggest a narrative similar to how Earth's moon is thought to have formed — as a result of a massive planetary impact between Mars and some other giant space rock, which broke off pieces of the planet that eventually coalesced to form the natural satellites that orbit there today.

Neither Phobos nor Deimos is spherical, isntead; both are oblong and lumpy, like potatoes. That fact — along with their chemical composition, as far as we have been able to tell using telescopic spectroscopy — point to the possibility that Phobos and Deimos were asteroids from the early solar system that were captured by Mars' gravitational pull. Figuring out the moons' true origin story would provide key clues about Mars' geological past, the solar system's early history and the formation of the inner planets, mission team members have said.

Once the MMX samples are safely returned to Earth, scientists will study their composition and mineralogy, then compare such chemical fingerprints with those of Martian rocks and asteroid material. These analyses, combined with data collected by MMX during its mission, will help nail down the origin of Phobos — and by extension, Deimos. — by

While JAXA leads MMX, the mission is an international effort, with interagency partnerships between JAXA, NASA and the European Space Agency (ESA), as well as U.S. and European companies, which supplied a handful of the spacecraft's scientific hardware and communications equipment.

NASA's contributions to MMX include the Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma rays and Neutrons (MEGANE, pronounced "meh-gah-nay") device, which is a gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer built by the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL); a Honeybee Robotics-built pneumatic sampler; and communications support using the agency's Deep Space Network.

NASA has also invested approximately $87 million through the end of the mission, which includes funding for United States scientists and astromaterials experts on the MMX team. The agency is getting something concrete for such contributions: At least 15% of the planned 10-gram (0.35 ounces) returned Phobos sample will be reserved for NASA's study. Those materials will be transferred and maintained at the agency's Johnson Space Center in Houston for analysis and long-term preservation.

MMX is not the first Phobos sample-return project to take flight, by the way. That distinction goes to Russia's Phobos-Grunt ("Phobos-Soil") mission, which launched in November 2011 but failed to get out of Earth orbit due to a rocket glitch. The 14.5-ton spacecraft eventually crashed back to Earth over the Pacific Ocean in January 2012.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 5 p.m. ET on Oct. 19 with news of MMX's successful separation from the H3 rocket's upper stage.

On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission arrived at Mars!

ExoMars 2016 consists of the Trace Gas Orbiter and the Schiaparelli lander. The orbiter and lander traveled there together and separated on Oct. 16, three days before the orbiter entered orbit around Mars, and the lander touched down on the planet's surface. But something went wrong during the lander's descent, and it crashed into the ground.

Schiaparelli did not survive the accident, but the Trace Gas Orbiter is still functional. It is currently circling the planet, looking for methane and other gases in the Martian atmosphere that could be evidence for possible biological activity.

Why it mattered

ExoMars 2016 was a landmark mission for the European Space Agency and designed to be the vanguard of a two-flight ExoMars program to send an orbiter, lander and rover to Mars.

Launched in March 2016, ExoMars 2016 aimed to achieve two goals for ESA and Russia. First, the mission aimed to use the Schiaparelli lander to test landing techniques that would be vital on a planned ExoMars 2018 rover. Second, the mission would deliver a critical orbiter around Mars to study the planet's atmosphere and serve as a communications link for that future Mars rover.

In the end, ExoMars 2016 was just a partial success, with ESA officials calling it "96% successful." due to the loss of the lander.

While Schiaparelli separated smoothly from the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter spacecraft, it stopped communicating with Earth just 1 minute before its planned landing on Oct. 19. Photos from NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter at Mars later revealed what appeared to be its crash site and, nearby, its jettisoned parachute. Officials suspect Schiaparelli did not fire its descent thrusters as designed in order to slow itself enough for a safe landing. A data glitch was cited as its cause.

The Trace Gas Orbiter, meanwhile, continues to study Mars to this day and has spent 10 years and counting studying the Martian atmosphere.

The launch of ExoMars 2018, which includes the Mars rover Rosalind Franklin, was delayed by the Schiaparelli failure, as well as the loss of its Russian Proton rocket when ESA severed its partnership with Russia over that country's war on Ukraine.

The ExoMars rover is now expected to launch no earlier than 2028, with a landing on Mars expected in 2030.

In 2026, another country took aim at Mars on this day.

The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency attempted to launch the ambitious Martian Moons eXploration mission (called MMX) to land a probe on the Mars moon Phobos and return samples to Earth.

]]> <![CDATA[ The moon is shrinking. 10,000 cracks on the lunar surface reveal by how much ]]> The moon is shrinking, and scientists are narrowing in on exactly how much our natural satellite has dwindled over the years.

The moon is thought to have formed from a violent collision between a massive object and our young Earth roughly 4.5 billion years ago, and its interior is still gradually cooling off from this ancient collision. As it cools, the moon contracts, leading to a long, slow shrinking process. Now, in a new study, scientists think that they have figured out how much smaller the moon is actually getting.

In this new study, scientists analyzing images snapped by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) have spotted over 10,000 young faults, or cracks across the moon's surface. This helped them to figure out how much the moon has contracted over time, and they now estimate that the moon's radius has decreased by about 148 feet (45 meters) over the past 400 to 800 million years.

"The number of these young faults revealed in LROC images is much greater than I ever imagined," study lead Thomas Watters, a geologist and scientist emeritus at the Center for Earth and Planetary Studies at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum, said in a statement. "As the interior of the moon continues to cool and contract, it is expected that the growth of existing faults and formation of new faults continues today."

With these LROC observations, researchers in this study saw a variety of different types of cracks and landforms across the lunar surface. This included lobate scarps, or long, curved structures that form when the moon's surface contracts, cracks and is pushed upwards; and small mare ridges, or narrow "wrinkles" in the lunar surface, across the dark plains on the moon.

Tectonic activity on the moon looks a lot different than it does on Earth. On our own planet, there are about 15 major tectonic plates. On the moon, there are no tectonic plates at all. Instead, the moon has a single-plate body meaning its outer shell is a single piece only broken by faults or other such cracks created by the moon contracting. This means that instead of faults or cracks appearing at tectonic plate boundaries, they are instead scattered all over the moon.

By mapping these thousands of different features, all created from the moon cooling and contracting over time, the researchers are piecing together lunar history. In addition to finding the extent to which the moon has shrunk over time, they also found that some areas of the moon are covered in many more faults than other areas, and the areas with fewer cracks and faults have thicker moon crust.

This led them to conclude that not only are these areas with thicker crust more stable, but they suggest that a great deal of the widespread cracks in the lunar surface were created later in the moon's history as, in its earlier years, its thick crust would have insulated the moon's warm interior and prevented cooling, contracting and cracking.

This work was described in a study published Oct. 14 in The Planetary Science Journal.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'They're kind of goth': NASA spacecraft gives mysterious brown dwarfs a close-up ]]> Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs.

These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars.

This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?). And that's apt, according to the leader of the new study, which reveals that, chemically speaking, the atmospheres of these dark and cloudy worlds are not unlike those of our solar system's gas giant planets.

"They’re kind of goth," Zafar Rustamkulov, of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement. "Unlike exoplanets, free-floating brown dwarfs are completely independent celestial objects that will fade into eternity alone. We’re still learning how complex they are."

Rustamkulov added that, from Earth orbit, SPHEREx — short for Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer — sees wavelengths of light that are nigh-impossible to see with telescopes on the ground because water in Earth’s atmosphere absorbs them. That is important for bringing brown dwarfs into the light.

"We are picking up light from the deep, red clouds of brown dwarfs all over the sky," he said.

A forest (of brown dwarfs)

Brown dwarfs have been somewhat mysterious since their discovery in the 1990s, due to the fact that the small amount of nuclear fusion that occurs within them causes them to emit no more than a faint glow. That means that our understanding of their makeup, their storms, and their evolution really only comes from theory.

To help lift this observational darkness, the team turned to data from SPHEREx. They studied 37 nearby brown dwarfs in a spectrum of light including 102 wavelengths, from the deepest red our eyes can see to the invisible infrared light. These local failed stars spanned the full temperature range for brown dwarfs — from 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit to minus 10 degrees Fahrenheit (2,200 to minus 20 degrees Celsius).

Considering that the temperature of the sun is about 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit (5,500 degrees Celsius), you could definitely say brown dwarfs run cold.

The spectra of brown dwarfs seen by SPHEREx allowed the team to determine that their atmospheres are chemically rich in water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and methane.

"We’re seeing the signatures of these molecules and how they change from object to object across the entire temperature regime," said team member J. Davy Kirkpatrick, also of Caltech. "Our paper concentrated on just three dozen, but we have thousands more that we are in the process of analyzing.

"I really want to see what bounds the universe places on the variety of brown dwarfs."

All my colors

Brown dwarfs have been routinely observed by other telescopes, including NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and the agency's now-retired Spitzer Space Telescope, but the wide wavelength coverage of SPHEREx has made it particularly useful in observing these failed stars. That's good news for astronomers waiting for change in the atmospheres of brown dwarfs as they age and grow cold.

The researchers found that some brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx are at a stage of extreme change in which their clouds are clearing, creating atmospheres rich in methane.

The team may have discovered significant new details about brown dwarfs, but they are still on the proverbial mystery street when it comes to these strange celestial objects,

"The state-of-the-art models are capturing the general chemical trend, but when it comes to these cloudy transitions, the models are struggling to match the data," said Rustamkulov. "No two brown dwarfs are alike. Even at the same temperature, their spectra look quite distinct."

"This journey has turned many of us into accidental meteorologists. We know how hard it is to predict weather on our own planet, and we realize it's going to be just as challenging to explain the phenomena we see in these bizarre, cold objects," Kirkpatrick said. "The findings are a call to action to explore even more of these dark worlds."

As astronomers resond to that call to action, I will ponder how I could have worked Bauhaus' Goth classic "Bela Lugosi is Dead" into this article.

The team's research was published on Sept. 28 in The Astrophysical Journal.

]]> <![CDATA[ Elephant Island is an icy sight from orbit | Space photo of the day for Oct. 19, 2026 ]]>

Antarctica is a magnificent sight, and that beauty is visible all the way from space.

What is it?

Orbiting planet Earth, the European Space Agency's (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-3 mission captured a close-up of West Antarctica.

Winter is ending in the Southern Hemisphere, meaning this is the peak of icy weather and sea ice in the Arctic.

In this image snapped by Sentinel-3, you can see a massive swath of ice which includes Elephant Island on the left-hand side. An ice-covered island off the Antarctic coast, Elephant Island floats in the Southern Ocean. It got its name both from the island's shape, which some liken to that of an elephant's head, and the fact that the island is home to a community of elephant seals.

Why is it incredible?

While a seal-inhabited island on the left floats near the Antarctic coast, across the water is a vast, frozen landscape. In just this snapshot, you can see about between 746 and 1,056 miles (1,200 to 1,700 kilometers) of the icy continent.

This image was captured on Sept. 30, 2026. In the Southern Hemisphere, that was just past the end of winter. The absolute peak for sea ice in Antarctica fell just a couple weeks before, on Sept. 14, according to the National Snow and Ice Data Center, ESA reported.

So in this one snapshot, we can see a near-maximum for sea ice in the Antarctic, spanning hundreds of miles. In observing our own planet from space, we are able to peer across vast landscapes, capturing important observational data. This is especially critical for the Antarctic as, with the progression of climate change, this sea ice continues to dwindle, adding to sea level rise among other serious consequences across the planet.

 <description>Univerzita Pardubice zatím nemůže začít vybírat zhotovitele stavby nové budovy Fakulty zdravotnických studií za víc než 300 milionů korun. Nemá totiž v tuto chvíli jistou dotaci. Ministerstvo školství sice vhodný dotační program chystá, zatím ho ale nevypsalo. Fakulta si tak na novou budovu nejspíš počká déle, než očekávala. <item>
 <title>Končí šéf zemědělského intervenčního fondu Dlouhý. ‚Jedná se o čistě osobní rozhodnutí,‘ říká</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/konci-sef-zemedelskeho-intervencniho-fondu-dlouhy-jedna-se-o-ciste-osobni_2610201405_vdv</link>
 <description>Ve funkci končí generální ředitel Státního zemědělského intervenčního fondu (SZIF) Petr Dlouhý. Fond to v úterý uvedl v tiskové zprávě, která Dlouhého cituje. Končící ředitel zdůrazňuje, že jde o „výhradně osobní rozhodnutí“, které „není výsledkem politických tlaků“. Dlouhý byl v SZIF přes 14 let, generálním ředitelem byl od roku 2022.</description>

 <description>Na koalici v Brně se dohodli vítězní lidovci a STAN, koalice ODS, TOP 09 a nezávislých, Zelené Brno, Piráti a hnutí Za Lužánky. Primátorem má být lídr koalice pěti uskupení Jakub Hruška. Zástupci stran to v úterý řekli novinářům. Koaliční smlouvu chtějí podepsat v pátek.</description>

<item>
 <title>Bytové nouzi čelí Liberecký kraj aktivně. Podporované bydlení majitelům zajistí prověřené nájemce a příjmy</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/bytove-nouzi-celi-liberecky-kraj-aktivne-podporovane-bydleni-majitelum-zajisti_2610200908_tez</link>
 <description>Liberecký kraj oslovuje majitele bytů prostřednictvím kampaně Bydlení je základ. Vlastníkům přitom nabízí odložit starosti s procesem hledání nájemníků a administrace jejich pobytu. Kampaň je součástí programu podporovaného bydlení, které se zaměřuje na lidi, kteří se ocitli v bytové nouzi. Pomocnou ruku nabízí nízkopříjmovým skupinám. Právě proto kraj hledá vlastníky nemovitostí, které by mohl lidem v nouzi nabízet.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Z odchodu spolustraníků ke KDU-ČSL viní Grolicha. ‚Rozbije to jednotu proti ANO,‘ říká Havel</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/z-odchodu-spolustraniku-ke-kdu-csl-vini-grolicha-jde-proti-snaze-spojit-se-proti_2610201219_nob</link>
 <description>Předseda jihomoravské TOP 09 Marek Sovka se rozhodl stranu opustit a přidat se ke KDU-ČSL. Stejně tak učiní i někteří další členové jihomoravské TOP 09. Podle Sovky stranu opustí asi 30 lidí, z nichž se někteří plánují přidat k lidovcům.
Řekl to v úterý novinářům na briefingu v Brně. Sovka uvedl, že nešlo o jednoduché rozhodnutí. Chce zároveň podpořit současného šéfa lidovců Jana Grolicha.</description>

   <title>Mohutná bouře se žene na Evropu, hrozí vichřice i obří vlny. Pocítí to i Česko</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/pocasi/pocasi-na-evropu-se-zene-obri-boure-vichrice-cesko-silny-vitr/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=pocasi</link>
   <description>Evropu čeká ve druhé polovině týdne bouřlivé počasí. Větrno bude také v Česku, kde meteorologové varují před silnými poryvy zejména v Jeseníkách, Beskydech a Bílých Karpatech.</description>

      <title>Poslanci jednají o návrhu, který zvyšuje tresty za týrání zvířat</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/snemovna-zakon-na-ochranu-zvirad-proti-tyrani-zakaz-lovu-norovanin.A261020_045902_domaci_kop#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Poslanci jednají o zvýšení trestů za týrání zvířat. Místo půlročního vězení za to má nově hrozit nejméně roční. Novela zavede i povinnost obcí zajišťovat na své náklady kastrace opuštěných a zdivočelých koček. Obce by se musely postarat o opuštěné domácí zvíře, které není zdivočelé a o něž nemá nikdo zájem.

</description>

      <description>V Kostelci nad Orlicí na Rychnovsku dnes po poledni podle policie šestačtyřicetiletý cizinec napadl a zabil mladou manželku. Podezřelého policisté na místě činu zadrželi do osmi minut. Šlo o pár z Kavkazu.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Smíchov znovuotevřel podnik podle návrhu sochaře Černého, víno vám nalije robotická ruka</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/praha/zpravy/smichov-roboticka-vinarna-cyberdog-david-cerny.A261020_144306_praha-zpravy_meli#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Na pražském Smíchově byla po několikaleté pauze znovuotevřena roboticky obsluhovaná vinárna Cyberdog. V restauraci postavené podle návrhu sochaře Davida Černého si lze objednat z mobilního telefonu, víno vám však nalije a přiveze robotická ruka.</description>

      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/103/cl6/MEL7dcd51b133_141839_15635233.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Otevření robotické vinárny CyberDog, která byla navržena sochařem Davidem Černým. Vinárna se po několikaleté pauze znovuotevřela díky spolupráci firmy Trigema a studentů Smíchovské střední, kteří robota naprogramovali. (20. října 2026)</media:description>

    <item>
      <title>Nepoučitelný spáč z Brtnice. Policie ho odvezla z cizí pergoly, brzy se vrátil</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/jihlava/zpravy/vysocina-brtnice-nezvany-host-policie-zatceni-dvakrat-spac.A261020_145625_jihlava-zpravy_epsal#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Nekonečným příběhem by se dala nazvat pondělní noc v Brtnici na Jihlavsku. Místnímu obyvateli se na zahradě u chaty usadil nezvaný host, který se po zásahu policie neváhal na stejné místo po pár hodinách vrátit. Zadržet ho tak museli dvakrát během jediné noci. Muži nyní hrozí za přečin porušování domovní svobody až dva roky vězení.</description>
      <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:16:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/jihlava/zpravy">Jihlava - Jihlava - zprávy</category>

      <guid isPermaLink="false">A261020_145625_jihlava-zpravy_epsal</guid>
      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/103/cl6/EPS7d8ec30998_stazeny_soubor.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Muž si na cizí zahradě v Brtnici udělal provizorní ležení. Když ho policie odvezla, vrátil se na stejné místo zpět.</media:description>
      <media:credit>Policie ČR</media:credit>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Za plentou vyfotíte lístek a dostanete za to peníze. Policie šetří kupčení s hlasy</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/volby/karlovy-vary/volby-komunalni-hlasy-kupceni-marianske-lazne-zabolotny.A261020_133049_vary-volby_pkz#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Možné kupčení s volebními hlasy šetří kriminalisté v Mariánských Lázních. Prověřují obvinění, podle něhož mladá žena za finanční odměnu organizovala hlasování ve prospěch politického hnutí Naše Česko. Klíčovým důkazem má být videozáznam z volebního víkendu, na němž byl vidět i ženin obličej, jak tvrdí zvolený zastupitel Samuel Zabolotný.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ukrajině nic neupíráme, Trump je z obvinění frustrovaný, řekl Rubio</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/ukrajine-nic-neupirame-trump-je-z-obvineni-frustrovany-rekl-rubio.A261020_145814_zahranicni_bro#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Není nic, co by Spojené státy Ukrajině záměrně upíraly, uvedl americký ministr zahraničí Marco Rubio během své návštěvy v Indii. Také řekl, že prezident USA Donald Trump je z obvinění, že Kyjevu záměrně škodí, frustrovaný. Trump nedávno navzdory protiruským sankcím nečekaně oznámil, že s Moskvou dohodl dodávky nafty na světové trhy. USA rovněž podle médií pohrozily Kyjevu, že jí přestanou poskytovat zpravodajské informace, pokud nezastaví útoky na ruské rafinerie.</description>

      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/generalni-reditel-zemedelskeho-fondu-dlouhy-konci-z-osobnich-duvodu-ve-funkci.A261020_140356_domaci_iluj#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Generální ředitel Státního zemědělského intervenčního fondu (SZIF) Petr Dlouhý končí v čele fondu, chce věnovat více času rodině a soukromému životu.     <item>
      <title>Německé město vystavilo sochu ďábla. Lidé se bouří, starostovi hrozí smrtí</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/nemecko-esslingen-socha-satan-dabel-s-cibuli-petice-kritika.A261020_111941_zahranicni_kha#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Rohy, kopyta, vypláznutý jazyk, zběsilý výraz ve tváři. A kolem hromada emocí. Bronzová socha ďábla v německém Esslingenu vystavená na náměstí vytočila část místních občanů tak, že proti ní sepsali petici. Poté, co někdo začal starostovi města vyhrožovat smrtí, se do kauzy vložila policie. Socha přitom vychází ze staré městské legendy a zastání našla i na překvapivém místě.</description>

      <media:description>Socha ďábla instalovaná na náměstí v německém Esslingenu vyvolala mezi místními vlnu nevole. (13. října 2026)</media:description>

    </item>

      <description>Přední tváře českého herectví, divadla i filmu bylo možno v úterý zahlédnout v prostorách Národního divadla. Čestnou stráž u jeho rakve postáli například František Němec, Zuzana Stivínová nebo manželé Petr Štěpánek a Zlata Adamovská.</description>

<item>
<title>Miton věří v AI agenty v e-commerce, miliony posílá do služby, která jim umožňuje hlídat ceny napříč trhem</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/miton-veri-v-ai-agenty-v-e-commerce-miliony-posila-do-sluzby-ktera-jim-umoznuje-hlidat-ceny-napric-trhem/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Dal&#353;í sázku na AI agenty v e-commerce vypsal Miton, který investuje do českého DeepScoutu, startupu, který právě otevírá svou databázi e-commerce dat umělé inteligenci. Ta je může využít k tvorbě vlastních cenových strategií, analýz a automatizací. Technologie DeepScoutu umí z e-shopů vytáhnout ceny, dostupnost i sortiment a poznat, které produkty si navzájem odpovídají. Doteď ji využívali hlavně velcí obchodníci včetně Alzy.</description>

 <title>Protestů ve Francii zneužívají organizované gangy vandalů, říká z Paříže podnikatelka</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/protestu-ve-francii-zneuzivaji-organizovane-gangy-vandalu-rika-z-parize_2610201355_vdv</link>
 <description>Zatím je příliš brzy na to říct, jestli masové protesty ve Francii nahrají krajní pravici, myslí si Lenka Girard, podnikatelka v Paříži a vystudovaná novinářka. „Kdekoliv (krajní pravice) vystoupí, konají se proti ní ohromné demonstrace,“ říká v rozhovoru pro Radiožurnál s odkazem na plánovaný sjezd v Orléans. Bezpečnostní opatření se podle ní vzhledem k dalším plánovaným demonstracím budou opakovat.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/img_7501_261018-201806_vdv.jpeg?itok=EL6IS8xR" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:55:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>‚Strašně ráda bych se vrátila.‘ Dívka musela s otcem utéct z Ruska kvůli kresbě protiválečného obrázku</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/strasne-rada-bych-se-vratila-divka-musela-s-otcem-utect-z-ruska-kvuli-kresbe_2610201200_vdv</link>
 <description>Maša Moskaljová nakreslila ve 12 letech ve škole v Jefremově, který leží asi 300 kilometrů jižně od Moskvy, protiválečný obrázek. Její otec Alexej musel kvůli tomu na dva roky do vězení a Maša do sirotčince. Když se vrátil, oba spolu uprchli do Francie. Americká stanice CNN natočila s Mašou rozhovor čtyři roky po události, která jí navždy změnila život.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-092136191_261020-124241_vdv.jpg?itok=LQOrDcJC" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>ONLINE: Chování Ruska vůči Ukrajině je v pořádku, moc jí toho nedělá, prohlásil Trump</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/donald-trump-rusko-ukrajina-chovani-ruska-vuci-ukrajine-v-poradku-vyrok_2610201033_ako</link>
 <description>„Rusko se vůči Ukrajině chová v pořádku. Moc toho nedělá,“ řekl americký prezident Donald Trump, když komentoval případné setkání lídrů USA, Ruska a Číny. To by se dle něj nekonalo kvůli Ukrajině. Slova pronesl ve stejný den, kdy ruský útok v Charkovské oblasti zabil šest lidí, z toho dvě děti. Předchozí noc Rusko zaútočilo na Kyjev více než tuctem balistických raket. Trump se ale k ničemu z toho nevyjádřil, uvedl server The Kyiv Independent.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-19t192715z_3_261020-101656_ako.JPG?itok=wPqIz1VK" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:33:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Alberta odmítla vykročit k odtržení od Kanady. Separatisté hledají podporu u Trumpových lidí</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/alberta-odmitla-vykrocit-k-odtrzeni-od-kanady-separatiste-hledaji-podporu-u_2610200843_ako</link>
 <description>Obyvatelé provincie Alberta si v referendu odhlasovali setrvání v Kanadě. Odmítli tak, aby vláda zahájila cestu k závaznému hlasování o odtržení. Průzkumy už předem ukazovaly, že většina rozpad země nechce. Separatisté se ale dlouhodobě sbližují s lidmi kolem amerického prezidenta Donalda Trumpa, který o Kanadě mluví jako o 51. státě USA.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-19t173637z_1_261020-081247_ako.JPG?itok=eAhvhnfq" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:43:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Kradené zboží z rabování ve Francii se objevilo za pár korun na internetu, portály ho blokují</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/kradene-zbozi-z-rabovani-ve-francii-se-objevilo-za-par-korun-na-internetu_2610200830_vdv</link>
 <description>V Paříži a dalších francouzských městech platily v noci zákazy vycházení. Místní prefektové je zavedli po jednání krizového štábu, který se sešel kvůli víkendovým násilnostem. Ministerstvo spravedlnosti také vyzvalo státní zástupce, aby případy hromadného rabování řešili jako organizovaný zločin.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-19t223805z_3_261020-073312_vdv.JPG?itok=CsDnteay" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:30:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Turistovi z Kanady hrozí v USA vězení za týrání zvířat. V opilosti unesl plameňáka a táhl ho po hotelu</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/turistovi-z-kanady-hrozi-v-usa-vezeni-za-tyrani-zvirat-v-opilosti-unesl_2610200729_vdv</link>
 <description>Kanadský turista, který odnesl plameňáka z výběhu v hotelu v Las Vegas, byl v pondělí shledán vinným z týrání zvířat, informuje v úterý agentura AP. Zatímco prokuratura čin označila za zlomyslný žert, obhajoba tvrdila, že šlo o opileckou hloupost a že muž plameňákovi nechtěl ublížit. Muži hrozí bezmála pět let vězení. Výše trestu bude oznámena v prosinci.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/20d9470913f2262936bce067b5e66fd3.jpg?itok=Q-IHOuKU" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 07:29:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Kremelští jestřábi si vychutnávají roztržku Trumpa a Zelenského. Šampaňské ale neotvírají</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-kremelsti-jestrabi-si-vychutnavaji-roztrzku-trumpa-a-zelenskeho-sampanske_2610200641_ako</link>
 <description>Kremelští jestřábi si vychutnávají veřejný rozkol mezi americkým prezidentem Donaldem Trumpem a jeho ukrajinským protějškem Volodymyrem Zelenským. Pro ukrajinskou hlavu státu byl uplynulý týden negativní, zatímco pro Rusko se vyvinul příznivě – přesto se v Moskvě šampaňské zatím stále chladí, píše agentura Reuters.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-09-25t164944z_6_261020-062851_ako.JPG?itok=v8S2hlT0" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 06:41:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Zpomalení Starlinku na Ukrajině? Musk vlastní oběžnou dráhu a Evropa zaspala, kritizuje analytik</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/zpomaleni-starlinku-na-ukrajine-musk-vlastni-obeznou-drahu-a-evropa-zaspala_2610200600_cen</link>
 <description>Amerika omezila satelity, Ukrajina mluví o tlaku na kapitulaci. Jak stěžejní je pro Zelenského a spol. družicový systém Starlink? A proč nemá Evropa svůj vlastní?</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/f6ea8b67b71e2e7c8a61a5ff1cbde225.jpg?itok=Lmk1DKRl" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 06:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Floridský soud vydal zatykač na Raúla Castra. Kubánská vláda obvinění vůči bývalému vůdci odmítá</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/floridsky-soud-vydal-zatykac-na-raula-castra-kubanska-vlada-obvineni-vuci_2610192204_jos</link>
 <description>Soud na Floridě vydal v pondělí zatykač na někdejšího kubánského vůdce Raúla Castra, a to na základě obvinění týkajícího se podílu na sestřelení dvou letounů kubánským vojenským letadlem v únoru 1996. Floridská prokuratura 95letého Castra obvinila ze spiknutí za účelem spáchání vraždy prvního stupně, píše web stanice NBC 6.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/castro_170617-062019_pla.jpeg?itok=cfP1TUP0" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 22:04:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Dav v indické Kolkatě zachvátila panika při oslavách Durgápúdžá. V provizorním chrámu zemřelo 19 lidí</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/dav-v-indicke-kolkate-zachvatila-panika-pri-oslavach-durgapudza-v-provizornim_2610192129_vaa</link>
 <description>Východ Indie slaví v těchto dnech nejdůležitější hinduistické svátky celého roku. Oslavy Durgápúdžá v Západním Bengálsku, které jsou zapsané i na seznamu UNESCO, ale poznamenala tragédie. V tlačenici u provizorního chrámu v Kolkatě zemřelo 19 lidí.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-18t000000z_1_261019-204415_vaa.JPG?itok=5BU82Zb7" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 21:29:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>

news.label: Kudyznudy
news.rawText:
Kudy z nudy – Žebříčky: Liberecký kraj Žebříčky RSS Feed <![CDATA[Dlabání dýní na Rychtě]]>

Už jste někdy nechali děti dlabat dýně v obýváku? Semínkový teror všude okolo je přesně ten důvod, proč se do toho doma raději nepouštět. Přijďte v neděli k nám! Připravili jsme správně velké dýně, které se dětem dobře dlabou, a jejich úklid zůstane na nás.

]]> Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:31:43 GMT <![CDATA[Folkrockový večer s Filipem Šimandlem a jeho synem]]>

Chytlavé autorské příběhy ze života, poctivý folkrock a jedinečné mezigenerační propojení! Přijďte si užít vystoupení písničkáře Filipa Šimandla, kterého na klávesy doprovodí jeho čtrnáctiletý syn. Vstupné 100 Kč.

]]> Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:18:59 GMT <![CDATA[Patrik Czuczor – Kytara napříč světem]]>

Vydejte se na hudební cestu od španělských mistrů a Latinské Ameriky až po ikonické hity Beatles nebo skupiny ABBA. Skvělý kytarový virtuóz Patrik Czuczor představí nádherné skladby i známé melodie ve vlastní úpravě. Vstupné 100 Kč.

]]> Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:16:25 GMT <![CDATA[Mňau Mňau Band]]>

Původně vznikli jen proto, aby nemuseli na trampském festivalu žádat o pomoc kamarády. Dnes mají na kontě ocenění z Porty a míří k nám! Přijďte si užít večer plný nadsázky, akordeonu a chytlavých autorských písniček. Vstupné 100 Kč.

]]> Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:12:53 GMT
